definition_zh: 火盆；烤肉炉；黄铜制品工
definition_en: a container for holding burning coal; also a worker in brass
core_image: 街头冬夜里一只黑铁火盆，炭火透红，双手围着火的人们凑近取暖
scene: 球赛散场的冷风里，摊主正收摊。The vendor warmed his hands over a small brazier of glowing coals.
sceneCN: 这里 brazier 是「火盆」（第 1 个义项：盛炭火的容器）；句意是摊主在一小盆烧得通红的炭火上烘手。

derivatives.zh: 由同根加形容词后缀构成，义为「黄铜制的；厚颜的」

senses.title: A pan for burning coal
senses.definition: a metal container in which coal or charcoal is burnt for warmth or cooking
senses.definitionCN: 用以烧煤取暖或烹饪的金属容器
senses.example: The night watch huddled around a brazier.
senses.exampleCN: 守夜人围着火盆挤作一团。
senses.why: The word first named the maker, then, by trade extension, the glowing pan he hammered out.
senses.whyCN: 该词先指匠人，后按行当延伸，转指他锤打出来的那只发红的火盆。

senses.title: An outdoor grill for cooking
senses.definition: an open pan over which food is grilled outdoors
senses.definitionCN: 户外架在火上烤食物的敞口炉
senses.example: Sausages hissed on the park brazier.
senses.exampleCN: 香肠在公园的烧烤炉上滋滋作响。
senses.why: Warmth for hands extends to heat for food; the pan stays, the purpose shifts.
senses.whyCN: 暖手之火延伸为烹食之火；盆还是那只盆，用途换了。

senses.title: A signal fire container
senses.definition: a raised brazier used to show light or smoke as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 架高以火光或烟为信号的火盆
senses.example: Hilltop braziers warned the next valley of invasion.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的火盆向下一个山谷示警敌袭。
senses.why: Fire raised high can speak across distances; the pan becomes a voice.
senses.whyCN: 高架之火能传话千里，火盆便成了声音。

senses.title: A ceremonial fire bowl
senses.definition: a decorative fire bowl used in rituals or processions
senses.definitionCN: 仪式或巡游中使用的装饰性火钵
senses.example: Priests swung braziers of incense before the altar.
senses.exampleCN: 祭司在祭坛前摇晃着香炉。
senses.why: The household pan dressed up for the gods becomes liturgy.
senses.whyCN: 家常的火盆为神明盛装后便成了礼器。

senses.title: A worker in brass
senses.definition: a craftsman who works brass into vessels, now historical
senses.definitionCN: 把黄铜打成器皿的工匠，今属历史用法
senses.example: The brazier's shop rang with hammer taps.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铜匠的铺子里锤声叮当。
senses.why: This was the word's first job in English, before it lent its name to the pan.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词在英语中的第一份差事，之后才把名字借给了火盆。

senses.title: A source of uncomfortable heat
senses.definition: figuratively, a place or situation of oppressive heat
senses.definitionCN: 比喻酷热难当之处或境地
senses.example: The packed courtroom was a brazier by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到正午，拥挤的法庭已热如火盆。
senses.why: The glowing pan maps onto any confined burning air.
senses.whyCN: 烧红的火盆被映射到一切闷闭灼热的空气。

senses.title: A gathering point of warmth
senses.definition: the brazier as the social center of a cold space
senses.definitionCN: 寒冷空间里以火盆为中心的聚点
senses.example: Stories were traded around the works brazier all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 一整个冬天，工地的火盆边故事不断。
senses.why: Fire draws bodies together; the object names the circle it creates.
senses.whyCN: 火把人聚拢，器物便命名了它围出的那个圈。

senses.title: Brazen brass, in old compound use
senses.titleCN: 与黄铜相关（旧复合用法）
senses.definition: in older compounds, marking things made of or like brass
senses.definitionCN: 旧复合词中标记黄铜制或似黄铜之物
senses.example: Braziers' work filled the church with gleaming vessels.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铜匠的活计让教堂里摆满闪亮的器皿。
senses.why: The trade sense keeps the metal itself in view, parent of the pan and the adjective brazen.
senses.whyCN: 行当义让人始终看见金属本身——火盆与形容词 brazen 的共同父母。

intro.en: Brazier comes from Old English bræs, brass, through the compound brazener, a worker in brass, later shifted to his product.
intro.cn: brazier 源自古英语 bræs（黄铜），经复合词 brazener（黄铜匠）而来，后转指其产品。

items.en: Old English bræs meant brass; its earlier origin is uncertain, possibly related to glass or burning words, but unresolved.
items.cn: 古英语 bræs 意为黄铜；更早来源不确定，或与玻璃、燃烧类词相关，尚无定论。

items.en: Bræs named the copper-zinc alloy prized for bright vessels.
items.cn: 古英语 bræs 指以色泽明亮器皿著称的铜锌合金。

items.en: Brazener, then brazier, named the craftsman who hammered brass.
items.cn: 十三世纪 brazener（后作 brazier）指锤打黄铜的工匠。

items.en: The live-coal pan took the maker's name, as smiths' products often borrowed smiths' titles.
items.cn: 十六世纪炭火盆借得匠人之名，如诸多工匠产品沿用匠人称号。

items.en: Street braziers warmed watchmen; hilltop braziers carried signals; the word traveled with fire.
items.cn: 街头火盆温暖守夜人，山头火盆传递信号；词随火而行。

items.en: Modern use centers on the cooking and warming pan; the craftsman sense is historical.
items.cn: 现代用法以取暖、烹食之盆为主；工匠义已成历史。

note.en: Brazier hides its cousin brass; its most dangerous twin is the proper name Brazil.
note.cn: brazier 藏着近亲 brass；最危险的孪生词是国名 Brazil。

entries.definitionCN: 黄铜制的；厚颜无耻的；同根形容词
巴西；仅一字母之差，纯为专名
法式小餐馆；与 brazier 词形相近，词源不同（法语 brewery 一族）

entries.definition: a sports jacket; a burning thing
entries.definitionCN: 运动外套；燃烧之物；拼写相近，词源不同
烤架；侧重烹具结构，brazier 侧重盛火容器
日式小火盆；同为便携炭炉
壁炉地面；brazier 是可移动的 Hearth

entries.definition: an open light or torch basket on a pole
entries.definitionCN: 高杆灯篮；旧时与信号火盆同用

entries.definition: an enclosed heating or cooking apparatus

normalIntro.en: Find brass inside: a brazier is the brass-worker's pan.
normalIntro.cn: 从 brass 入手：brazier 就是黄铜匠的火盆。

normal.en: brass is the metal root of the family.
normal.cn: brass 是词族的金属词根。

normal.en: the first brazier hammered brass, not coal.
normal.cn: 最初的 brazier 敲打黄铜，不碰炭火。

normal.en: the pan borrowed the smith's name by trade custom.
normal.cn: 火盆按行当惯例借了匠人之名。

normal.en: brazen, brazenly bold, shares the brass root.
normal.cn: brazen（厚颜的）也出自 brass 词根。

normal.en: watch the single z: brazier, not Brazil.
normal.cn: 注意只有一个 z：是 brazier，不是 Brazil。

abstract.en: A red eye glowing in the dark street.
abstract.cn: 黑街上睁开的一只红眼睛。

abstract.en: Hands outstretched in a circle, shadows leaning in.
abstract.cn: 围成一圈伸出的手，影子向内倾。

abstract.en: Fire kept in a pan, like a pet that must be fed.
abstract.cn: 火被关进盆里，像一只必须喂养的宠物。

examples.en: Street singers warmed their fingers over a shared brazier.
examples.cn: 街头艺人们围着一只共用的火盆烘手。

examples.en: The garden brazier glowed long after the guests had gone.
examples.cn: 客人散尽后，庭园的火盆仍亮了很久。

examples.en: Medieval braziers beat out church doors and candlesticks in gleaming brass.
examples.cn: 中世纪的黄铜匠打制出闪亮的教堂门饰与烛台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不累热」——围着火盆取暖，身子「不累」又「热」乎：brazier 就是那只让人不累又热的盆。

root: 古英语 bræs（黄铜；更早来源不确定）+ 表人复合词 brazener（黄铜匠）→ 中古英语 brazier；十六世纪起由「匠人」转指「火盆」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moved from the smith who worked brass to the glowing pan he made, then outward to grills, signals, rites, and figurative heat.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义由打铜的匠人移至其打出的火盆，再扩展至烤炉、信号、礼仪及比喻性的灼热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pan of live coals glowing in the cold open air
core.cn: 核心意象：寒天露天里一盆烧得通红的炭火

branches.en: the warm circle: coals, muggy heat, gathered hands
branches.cn: 温暖的圆圈：炭火、闷热、拢起的手

branches.en: from warmth to food: the pan becomes a grill
branches.cn: 由暖到食：火盆变身烤炉

branches.en: fire raised high: signals to valleys, incense to gods
branches.cn: 高架之火：向山谷报警，向神明进香

branches.en: the smith remembers: brass in the worker's hands
branches.cn: 匠人的记忆：匠人手中的黄铜

branches.en: the heat made felt: a room become a brazier
branches.cn: 可感的灼热：一室化为火盆

intro.en: The formation is trade-English: metal name plus worker suffix, later loaned to the product.
intro.cn: 构词属行当英语：金属名加表人后缀，后转借给产品。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates are established; brass's deeper history remains open.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确定的拉丁同源词；brass 的更深层历史仍是开放问题。

items.exampleCN: 古英语金属工艺词 bræs
hibachi 与 brazier 功能相当

items.example: cressets and braziers both carried fire
items.exampleCN: cresset 与 brazier 都承载火
brasserie 源自法语 brasser（酿酒）
